questions.title: Which country will become the second, after the United States, to formally recognise Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights by the end of 2026?
questions.background: The United States formally recognised Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights in 2019. Most of the international community has rejected Israel’s annexation of the territory.

local_articles.title: Colombia's new president to take office in ceremony highlighting hard line on armed groups
local_articles.snippet: BOGOTA, Colombia — Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella will be sworn in as Colombia’s president Friday under heavy security in Cali, a city in the country’s volatile southwest, breaking with the tradition of holding the ceremony in the capital, in a move meant to signal his hard-line approach to illegal armed groups De la Espriella, 48, will succeed Gustavo Petro after winning a close runoff election on June 21 against the outgoing president’s ally, Sen. Iván Cepeda. De la Espriella, who has never held public office before, ran as an outsider, financing his campaign with the fortune he amassed as a lawyer and businessman. His inauguration, to be held at a university auditorium before Congress, marks a further shift to the right in the region . questions.title: Which stadium will Shakhtar Donetsk announce an agreement to use for its home matches in the main phase of the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League?
questions.background: War has prevented Shakhtar Donetsk from hosting European matches in Ukraine, forcing the club to arrange alternative venues abroad.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Shakhtar Donetsk announcement, or reliable reporting quoting the club, identifying its agreed home venue for the 2026–27 Champions League main phase. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the stadium named in the first such agreement announced by August 31, 2026. The announcement determines the answer; subsequent regulatory approval or the actual staging of matches is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The stadium’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Complete venue overhaul driven by June 24 - July 26 reporting (BBC Sport, City AM, The Athletic via talkSPORT, Evening Standard, and UNN/Suspilne Sport): Shakhtar officially stated they are negotiating with venues in the UK and Germany (dropping Poland after Wisla Krakow's refusal), and on July 26 Shakhtar head coach Arda Turan explicitly announced 'It looks like we will play our European Cup matches in London... We are also waiting for everyone in London.' Three West London Premier League clubs with no 2026-27 European football have held talks: Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium (0.28 — earliest/longest-documented talks since June 24, established third-party rental model, UEFA compliant), Chelsea's Stamford Bridge (0.26 — 40k turnkey UCL venue, Chelsea seeking non-European revenue after finishing 10th), and Fulham's Craven Cottage (0.23 — renovated Riverside Stand and strong Shakhtar-Fulham relationship from the Kevin transfer). Keeping Veltins-Arena (0.06) as the top German fallback if London policing/council permits stall, and London Stadium (0.04) as an unconfirmed London UEFA Cat 4 fallback with West Ham in the Championship (sum 0.87, leaving 13% for other German/London venues).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-06 update (AP News Aug 6, L'Express Europe Aug 6, local CBS News Aug 5): Neither Romania nor Hungary has yet announced initiation of a full shutdown of its last operating reactor (confirming PM Peter Magyar's Aug 1 warning did not trigger full shutdown as Paks stayed online on one unit). Today's reporting widens Romania's lead as the likeliest country to announce a complete drought-related nuclear shutdown between Aug 1 and Aug 13: AP News reports on Thursday Aug 6 that Romania is still racing to sink four rock-filled barges into the Danube 'to buy more time before its second reactor is likely forced offline due to record-low water levels,' with Cernavoda sitting 1,200 km downstream facing the arriving low-water trough. Meanwhile, Hungary's Paks has survived through Thursday on its earlier +5 cm water reprieve with a Friday Aug 7 cold front arriving tomorrow, though a 10-day dry forecast keeps Paks substantially at risk. Lifting Romania 0.54 -> 0.58 and trimming Hungary 0.40 -> 0.35. Also nudging Slovenia 0.01 -> 0.02 after L'Express (Aug 6) reported Slovenia's sole nuclear plant (Krsko) is cutting output to 80% due to low/warm river levels, keeping Bulgaria (Kozloduy on lower Danube) at 0.035 and Switzerland at 0.005 (sum 0.99).
